ROLE-002.summary: Private teams.** An Admin can make a team private. Its issues, comments, attachments, cycles, triage, project memberships and search entries are visible only to its members and to Owners; a project or initiative that spans a private team shows other viewers only the counts they may see, never titles. Making a team public or private is audited and re-evaluates notifications, followers, Slack channel routes and webhooks. Inherited from WORK-004: after a member loses access to a private-team issue, it is absent from Created, Subscribed and Activity; the private-team journey checks every tab. Inherited from SLACK-003: private-team content posts only to channels an Admin bound to that team; its acceptance journey verifies that project and saved-view bindings cannot bypass this rule. SLACK-003 channel posts and SLACK-004 direct messages for private/restricted items use only a generic notice without actor or text, or a DM to a permitted explicitly mapped member; its acceptance proves this before private teams ship. Current status: missing.

ROLE-011.summary: Suspend and reactivate members.** Suspension is the default offboarding: Settings → Members' Suspend action (Owners and Admins; only an Owner suspends an Owner or Admin), a member's own Leave workspace, and SCIM `PATCH` with `active: false` or `DELETE` on the user (ROLE-004) all produce the same suspended state, which takes effect on the member's next request. It revokes every session on every device, every personal API token (API-001), every OAuth grant they authorized (API-004) and the MCP sessions under them (AGENT-005), every passkey (ROLE-010), every mobile, desktop and Web Push registration (MOBILE-002, MOBILE-005), and their linked Slack, Teams and GitHub identities (SLACK-001, SLACK-004, TEAMS-001, GITHUB-006), so a suspended member's SLACK-004 link is deleted, no Slack direct message reaches them and a signed Slack action from their account is refused; magic-link, Google and SSO sign-in for that email are refused while they are suspended. A suspended member no longer counts in the member count or any seat limit, cannot be mentioned, assigned, added to a team or project, or delegated work, and receives no notification or digest; their team memberships and team ownerships are kept but inactive, and a team left with no active team owner is managed by Admins until one is named (ROLE-007). Their name stays, labeled "Suspended", on every comment, description revision, activity entry, audit entry (ROLE-005), project update and customer request they wrote and on their profile, which Owners and Admins open from the member directory's Suspended filter to see their issue activity; the directory lists suspended members apart from active ones. In the same dialog the person suspending chooses whether the member's non-terminal issues stay assigned (each flagged "Assignee suspended" in lists, Current and the Members page for reassignment) or are unassigned; projects they led and shared views they owned transfer as OPS-004 states; their private saved views, favorites and drafts are kept hidden and return on reactivation; and coding-agent sessions they delegated (AGENT-001) are paused and listed for an Admin to reassign or cancel. Reactivation — by an Owner or Admin from the Suspended filter (only an Owner reactivates a former Owner or Admin), by SCIM `active: true`, or by inviting the same email again — restores the same member record and ID with its role, history, team memberships and private views; it never restores a revoked session, token, OAuth grant, passkey, push registration or linked identity, so the member signs in afresh. Suspension, leaving and reactivation each write one audit entry with the actor and the method (Settings, self or SCIM), and neither suspension nor any SCIM call anonymizes anything (ROLE-012). The portable export (DATA-001) carries each member's state with the suspension time and actor, and a restore (DATA-005) brings a suspended member back suspended, with no session or credential. Current status: partial.

PROJ-010.summary: Project updates.** The project's lead and members (PROJ-014), Owners and Admins post dated updates (Guests cannot, role matrix) with a status of On track, At risk or Off track and a Markdown body; Vector prefills the draft with computed health (PROJ-005), progress since the last update, completed and newly added scope, and slipped milestones. Updates appear in the project, roll up into initiatives (INIT-002), notify project followers, and post to the project's Slack or Teams channel (SLACK-003). Leads are reminded on the project's cadence (AUTO-005). Computed health and the lead's stated status are shown side by side, never merged. Inherited from NOTIFY-001: a followed project or initiative update notifies once in the inbox, never the actor; the receiving journey verifies this before the event ships. Inherited from SLACK-003: each project update posts to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, using the shared durable delivery and minimal-message rules; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

INIT-001.summary: Initiatives.** An initiative groups projects (and sub-initiatives up to three levels) under an owner, description, target date and status (Planned, Active, Completed), across teams. A project can belong to several initiatives. Owners, Admins and Members create and edit initiatives and add projects to them; Guests cannot (role matrix). Inherited from SLACK-003: initiatives bind chosen events to a Slack or Discord channel and each event posts to its bound channel once, using the shared durable delivery and minimal-message rules; its acceptance journey verifies the binding and bound post. Current status: missing.

RELEASE-001.summary: Releases.** Owners, Admins and Members define team or workspace releases (versions) — a Member a team's releases only for teams they can see, and Guests none (role matrix) — each with name, target date, status (Planned, In progress, Released) and description; issues and projects join a release; a release page shows scope, progress, blockers and linked PRs, and can be shared read-only inside the workspace. Jira fix versions import as releases. Inherited from SLACK-003: a release posts to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, using the shared durable delivery and minimal-message rules; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

RELEASE-003.summary: Release notes.** For a release or a date range, Vector drafts internal release notes from completed issues grouped by label or project, using each issue's title and an optional "release note" field, which the release owner edits and publishes to the workspace, Slack, or hands to Penny as a changelog draft. Inherited from SLACK-003: publishing release notes posts the release event to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, without duplicating RELEASE-001’s post; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

NOTIFY-007.summary: Channels and digests.** Each member chooses per event type whether it reaches them in the inbox only, by email, in a Slack or Teams direct message, by mobile push, or as a desktop notification (MOBILE-005), and can take email as an immediate message or an hourly or daily digest; Admins set workspace defaults. Working hours gate every time-of-day digest delivery. Digests follow the member's personal time zone and working hours (NOTIFY-010): a daily digest is sent once at the start of the member's working hours on each working day, and hourly digests are sent only within working hours, with anything collected outside them carried into the next digest. Every channel honors mutes (NOTIFY-004), actor exclusion (NOTIFY-003) and access (OPS-001), and never repeats a delivered notification. SLACK-004 delivers Slack direct messages for assignments and mentions now, the events NOTIFY-006 mails; the per-event choice for every other event, Admin defaults, digests, mobile push (MOBILE-002), desktop notifications (MOBILE-005) and Teams direct messages (TEAMS-001) remain this clause's. Current status: partial.

AUTO-004.summary: SLAs.** Teams set SLA targets by priority, label or customer tier (for example: Urgent bugs from Enterprise customers resolved in 24 hours, triage within 4 business hours in the workspace timezone); issues show time remaining, warn the assignee and triage owner before breach, and record breaches for reporting (REPORT-001). Inherited from NOTIFY-001: an SLA warning notifies once in the inbox, never the actor; the receiving journey verifies this before the event ships. Inherited from SLACK-003: an SLA warning posts to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, using the shared durable delivery and minimal-message rules; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

SLACK-001.summary: Slack app.** Each installation has its own Slack app, created from Settings → Integrations → Slack through Slack's app manifest (INTEG-001's table): with a one-time app configuration token Vector calls `apps.manifest.create` with the generated manifest (this installation's event, interactivity, slash-command, unfurl and OAuth redirect URLs and least scopes) and receives the app's credentials; without a token, Vector opens Slack's create-from-manifest page prefilled and the Admin pastes the signing secret, client ID and client secret Slack shows. The Admin then clicks Install, which completes OAuth v2 to the company's Slack workspace (or an Enterprise Grid org) and stores the bot token encrypted. Members link their Slack identity to their Vector member; uninstalling or unlinking stops all calls and removes stored tokens. Inherited from SEC-001: credentials are sealed, shown once, least-scoped, excluded from archives, re-entered on restore, rotated on demand and revoked on removal; an archive-then-restore journey proves no credential is exported and the restored connection needs re-entry. SLACK-003 already covers the sealed bot-token paste path and its archive/re-entry proof; SLACK-004 covers member-confirmed linking by the member's own sign-in email, the pasted signing secret and the interactivity door; the manifest/OAuth installation, Events API, @Vector issue creation, explicit Admin mapping and uninstall remain this clause’s acceptance. Current status: missing.

SLACK-003.summary: Channel notifications.** Teams, projects, initiatives and saved views can post chosen events (new triage item, new issue, status change, project update, release, SLA warning, agent completion) to a Slack channel, respecting ROLE-002 so private-team content only posts to channels the Admin bound to that team. A team or project can create its own Slack channel when it is created (`conversations.create`, named from its identifier or name) and bind it automatically, and a Discord channel can receive the same events through a Discord webhook URL. An Admin enters a Slack bot token in Settings → Integrations once; auth.test validates it, sealSecret/openSecret seal it per workspace, settings never reveal it again, archives exclude it, restored installations need attention until re-entry, and removal calls auth.revoke, deletes local custody and disables bindings (a provider error refuses removal visibly). Until ROLE-001 every admitted operator acts as Admin; no private teams exist, so every team is workspace-visible and bindable, and ROLE-002 inherits the private-team channel restriction before private teams ship. Existing new-triage, new-issue and status-change events post through the shared native outbound claim, bounded-retry, uncertain-result and visible Settings failure machinery, once per event per binding. Saved-view membership uses the same list predicates at dispatch. Messages carry identifier, title, readable actor, old → new status and the canonical /app/issues/:identifier link, never description or comment bodies. Unbinding, issue deletion and operator removal stop future posts; already-posted Slack or Discord messages cannot be recalled by local erasure (SEC-003). Channel creation makes one conversations.create call with a lowercase hyphenated identifier or name of at most 80 characters, public channels only; name_taken and other Slack errors are shown without a retry loop and refuse object creation. Discord accepts only HTTPS discord.com or discordapp.com URLs whose path starts /api/webhooks/, seals the URL and refuses redirects; this fixed-host rule does not depend on arbitrary resolved-address egress. PROJ-010, RELEASE-001/RELEASE-003, AUTO-004, AGENT-002/AGENT-003 and INIT-001 inherit their future objects’ bound-channel events and acceptance before shipping. Slack channel selection and each post explicitly check conversations.info: bot membership and is_channel true, archived/shared/external-shared/org-shared/pending-external-shared false, and not frozen; the held Slack conversation object omits is_frozen, recorded as an assumption that an absent is_frozen means not frozen (revisable if a provider run contradicts it). Unsafe channels and archived/frozen/not-joined post refusals suspend routing visibly until an Admin confirms a fresh binding; held events are not replayed. Channel IDs are explicitly mapped by the Admin, never inferred from email or name. Actor display names are allowed for current workspace-visible items (ct, 20 Oct 19:12Z); ROLE-002 inherits generic notices without actor or text, or a DM to a permitted explicitly mapped member, for private/restricted items before they ship. Current status: done.

SLACK-004.summary: Personal Slack notifications.** Members can receive their notifications as Slack direct messages under NOTIFY-007 with actions (assign to me, change status, open). A signed-in member chooses Link Slack in Settings → Notifications; Vector calls `users.lookupByEmail` (scope users:read.email) with that member's own Vector sign-in email, shows the Slack account it found and links it only when the member confirms; no match shows "No Slack account found for this email" and stores nothing, and a lookup error is shown and not retried. There is no silent or background lookup, no lookup by an Admin for someone else's email, no bulk directory read (`users.list`) and no matching on names (ct, 20 Oct 19:12Z); explicit Admin mapping remains SLACK-001's. The link is shown, audited (`slack.member_linked`, `slack.member_unlinked`) and revocable with Unlink; unlinking, member removal, suspension (ROLE-011 inherits) and removal of the workspace's Slack credential delete it and stop every direct message. A linked member turns on Slack direct messages separately for assignments and for direct mentions, the events Vector mails today (NOTIFY-006); the option is unavailable, with the reason shown, while the workspace has no valid Slack credential or the member has no link, and NOTIFY-007 keeps the choice for every other event. Each qualifying notification creates at most one direct-message intent per recipient in the same transaction as its source mutation, in the native outbound ledger (no second queue); immediately after commit, like immediate mail, and before every later attempt Vector rechecks mutes (NOTIFY-004), actor exclusion (NOTIFY-003), the active recipient, issue access (OPS-001) and the member's link and choice, then calls `conversations.open` (im:write) and `chat.postMessage`. A delivered message is never repeated: rate limits and an unanswered `conversations.open` (which posts nothing) retry at most three attempts, after one and then five minutes; an unknown `chat.postMessage` result is uncertain and never resent; failed and uncertain messages are listed to the recipient in Settings → Notifications. A message carries only the event kind, issue identifier and title, actor display name, status change, due date and the authenticated canonical `/app/issues/:identifier` link, in plain-text blocks with `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` false — never a description, comment or mention body, free text or AI output; private or restricted items (none exist until ROLE-002) get a generic notice with no actor or text under ROLE-002. Open is the canonical link button; Assign to me and Change status (an inline select of the team's workflow states the issue-edit door accepts) appear only while the workspace's Slack signing secret is stored, and Settings says they are off until it is entered (pattern 3). Slack's interactivity requests reach `POST /api/integrations/slack/interactive`, which verifies `X-Slack-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<raw body>`) in constant time, refuses a timestamp more than 5 minutes from the Worker clock and a replayed request key, maps the Slack user to the Vector member only through the confirmed link and runs the change through the version-checked issue-edit door with that member's own authority and the issue version the message carried. A changed issue is refused with a threaded Slack reply carrying Open and is never overwritten; an applied change refreshes the message with the new version. The door answers before Slack's 3-second limit and replies afterwards. An unlinked, removed or suspended Slack user, a bad or missing signature, a stale timestamp and a replay change nothing. An Admin enters the Slack app's signing secret beside the bot token in Settings → Integrations; it is sealed with sealSecret/openSecret per workspace, never shown again, excluded from archives with the member links (SEC-001: after a restore it is entered again and members re-link) and removed with the credential. docs/INTEGRATIONS.md names the Interactivity Request URL the Admin sets in their Slack app until SLACK-001's manifest sets it, and what leaves the deployment in a direct message. Current status: done.

AGENT-002.summary: Agent session on the issue.** Each delegation opens an agent session shown on the issue, fed by the provider mechanism of AGENT-009, with live progress (plan, steps, files touched, commands run, elapsed time and cost in USD when the provider reports it), questions the agent asks a person (answered in the issue or Slack), and a cancel action that stops the session within one minute and records who stopped it. Where a provider has no mid-run question channel, the session says so and a member's answer starts a follow-up run on the same branch (AGENT-009). Inherited from NOTIFY-001: a delegated agent question or completion notifies once in the inbox, never the actor; the receiving journey verifies this before the event ships. Inherited from SLACK-003: agent completion posts to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, using the shared durable delivery and minimal-message rules; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

AGENT-003.summary: Reviewable output, human completion.** An agent's work lands as a branch and pull request linked to the issue (GITHUB-003), with the tests it added or ran and a summary; the issue moves to In Review, never to Completed, until a person reviews and merges the PR and the team rule or a person completes the issue. An agent may not merge, deploy, change priority, due date or assignee, or message a customer. Inherited from SLACK-003: reviewable agent completion posts to its bound Slack or Discord channel once, without duplicating AGENT-002’s completion event; its acceptance journey verifies the bound post. Current status: missing.

SEC-001.summary: Integration credentials.** Every integration and agent credential (GitHub App keys, Slack and Teams tokens, provider API tokens, OAuth refresh tokens) is stored encrypted, shown once, scoped to the least access the feature needs, excluded from archives, re-entered on restore, rotated on demand and revoked when the integration is removed. The Slack bot-token paste path (SLACK-003), the Slack signing secret and member-confirmed Slack links (SLACK-004) and Discord webhook URLs are covered now. SLACK-001’s manifest/OAuth install, Events API, @Vector issue creation and explicit identity linking beyond the member-confirmed email link remain SLACK-001’s. SLACK-001, GITHUB-006 and AGENT-004 inherit these credential rules and their provider archive/re-entry acceptance cells before they ship. Current status: done.

agentUpdateInstructions: Upgrade from 0.4.0: stop local development by its own PID, export a backup, preserve owner customizations and all applied SQL, pull this release, run rer install and rer dev. On own-account hosting back up with the authenticated transfer client, pull the release and rer deploy using the existing environment and deployment custody. Pin @runeditrun/rer 0.2.77. Apply 0073–0074 in order after unchanged 0001–0072. A local backup or restore of a database Run Edit Run Platform migrated (rer_migrations ledger) no longer runs Wrangler; Platform must have applied every migration first, otherwise the transfer refuses with migration_ledger:unapplied:<file> and changes nothing. Slack and Discord credentials are excluded from archives: re-enter them and re-link Slack members after a restore. Retain all additive tables, terminal effects and delivery ledgers on compatible-source rollback. Restore into isolated empty resources and re-enter excluded credentials before changing traffic.
publicReleaseNotes:
Vector 0.4.1 restores backups into installations whose database Run Edit Run Platform migrated. Such a database records its migrations in Platform's ledger, which Wrangler cannot read; a local restore or backup used to run Wrangler anyway and stopped at "Preparing archive schema" with "table workspace_settings already exists". Vector now leaves that database to Platform's runner, checks that every migration is applied, and restores the listed version's backups and its own with every archived row, cell and file intact, into Platform-migrated and native installations alike. This release uses rer 0.2.77.

Teams, projects and saved views can post new triage items, new issues and status changes to a Slack channel or a Discord webhook, and a team or project can create its own Slack channel. Members can link their Slack account and receive assignments and mentions as Slack direct messages with Assign to me, Change status and Open actions. Messages carry the identifier, title, actor and status change, never descriptions or comments; credentials are sealed and never travel in backups. TanStack Start is patched for GHSA-qx66-fv34-fjm8.

Apply migrations 0073–0074 after unchanged 0001–0072. Back up before upgrading; retain additive schema and delivery ledgers on rollback.

Known limits: roles, private teams, guests and most provider integrations remain incomplete as shown in CONTRACT.md; Slack app installation through its manifest, @Vector issue creation and Teams are not available. Linear and Jira importers are documented-format, synthetic-only; there is no Asana importer. Managed mail relay and broad capacity are not claimed. Local setup and development still migrate with Wrangler; a local database carrying Platform's migration ledger is for backup and restore only. For hosted backups use the authenticated Base transfer client described in CHANGELOG.md.
